title: La ilaha illallah
hook: the heaviest words on the scale, no god but Allah

segments.voice: Yesterday: Allahu akbar, thirty-four, the gift to Fatimah. Your line was better than a servant. Today, one sentence on a scale.

A scale, the old kind, two pans hanging from a beam. On one side: ninety-nine scrolls, records of things they did wrong, each one, the story says, stretching as far as the eye can see. The pan crashes down. On the other side, someone places one small card, a few words written on it. The scale swings the other way. The scrolls fly up. The card is heavier. It's a hadith, in the collection of at-Tirmidhi. Today: the words on the card.
screen: `NINETY-NINE SCROLLS.` → `ONE SMALL CARD.` → `THE CARD IS HEAVIER.`

segments.voice: On the card is the testimony of faith, and its heart is the first half: la ilaha illallah. There is no god but Allah. Saying it is called tahlil. You've met these words inside the shahada, the first pillar, in the call to prayer, and at the end of the hundred after the prayer, three days ago. But look at how the sentence is built. It starts with a no. La ilaha: there is no god. Every idol, cleared away first. Some teachers read it more widely: anything a person serves without calling it worship, like money or approval. Then, illallah: except Allah. Only one comes back. Scholars call the two halves the negation and the affirmation. You empty the room, then let one in. The Qur'an puts the same idea in Surah al-Ikhlas, four short verses, which in Pickthall's translation reads: "Say: He is Allah, the One! Allah, the eternally Besought of all! He begetteth not nor was begotten. And there is none comparable unto Him." A hadith in Tirmidhi calls la ilaha illallah the best remembrance. One in Abu Dawud says that whoever's last words are la ilaha illallah will enter Paradise. And that's the point of the card. Ninety-nine scrolls of mistakes, and one sentence underneath them all: I knew there was only one. In the tradition, that sentence, meant truly, weighs more than all the rest.
screen: `TAHLIL — NO GOD BUT ALLAH.` · `FIRST, A NO.` · `THEN ONE COMES BACK.` · `SAY: HE IS ALLAH, THE ONE.` · then, large: `THE CARD OUTWEIGHS THE SCROLLS.`

segments.voice: Say it ten times, slowly, counting on your fingers: on la ilaha, breathe out and let go of one thing that takes up more of your mind than it should; on illallah, breathe in. If you pray, say the Arabic; if you don't, breathe the shape of it, out, letting go, in, one thing left. Then rest the hand and stay quiet.
Tahlil. Saying la ilaha illallah, there is no god but Allah: a no that clears the room, and a yes. Today's word.
Your line: there is only one. Everything else can go back in its place. Day one hundred seventeen, done.

howItsDone: Muslims say la ilaha illallah as dhikr after prayers and through the day, often counted on the fingers or beads, and hope it will be the last words on their lips before death.

original.note: Arabic: there is no god but Allah. tahlil (تَهْلِيل) is saying it.

trapdoor: what you thought: la ilaha illallah is a Muslim slogan.
what it means: a no that clears away every other god, then a yes to one; the heaviest words on the scale.
what a scholar hears: nafy and ithbat, negation and affirmation; the hadith of the card (Tirmidhi 2639); and 'the best dhikr' (Tirmidhi 3383).

notes: Hadith numbers cited from memory; please confirm. In the hadith of the card, the card bears the full shahada (including 'Muhammad is His servant and messenger'); the script says the card holds the testimony and that its heart is the first half.
The list 'money, approval, fear, a person, a phone' as things people worship is an interpretive gloss; a Keeper may want to soften it.
